The previous behavior unconditionally disabled worktree isolation whenever `.gitmodules` existed, which penalised every quick task in a submodule project even when the task was nowhere near a submodule. Parse submodule paths from `.gitmodules` so the executor can act on actual submodule paths rather than the mere file's existence:\n164\t\n165\t```bash\n166\t# Parse submodule paths from .gitmodules once (empty if no .gitmodules).\n167\t# SUBMODULE_PATHS is a newline-separated list of repo-relative paths used as\n168\t# a fail-loud commit-time guard inside the quick-task executor — if the\n169\t# executor stages any path that falls inside SUBMODULE_PATHS, it must abort\n170\t# the commit and surface the conflict rather than silently corrupting the\n171\t# submodule state.\n172\tif [ -f .gitmodules ]; then\n173\t  SUBMODULE_PATHS=$(git config --file .gitmodules --get-regexp '^submodule\\..*\\.path$' 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $2}')\n174\telse\n175\t  SUBMODULE_PATHS=\"\"\n176\tfi\n177\t```\n178\t\n179\tQuick mode does not have a pre-declared `files_modified` list (the task is freeform), so use a fail-loud guard at commit time: when the executor stages files for the quick-task commit, if any staged path falls inside a `SUBMODULE_PATHS` entry, abort with a clear error explaining that worktree-isolated commits cannot safely span submodule boundaries — the user can re-run with `workflow.use_worktrees=false` to fall back to sequential execution on the main tree. If `SUBMODULE_PATHS` is empty (no `.gitmodules` in the repo), worktree isolation proceeds normally.\n180\t\n181\t**If `roadmap_exists` is false:** Error — Quick mode requires an active project with ROADMAP.md. Run `/gsd-new-project` first.\n182\t\n183\tQuick tasks can run mid-phase - validation only checks ROADMAP.md exists, not phase status.\n184\t\n185\t---\n186\t\n187\t**Step 2.5: Handle quick-task branching**\n188\t\n189\t**If `branch_name` is empty/null:** Skip and continue on the current branch.\n190\t\n191\t**If `branch_name` is set:** Check out the quick-task branch before any planning commits.\n192\t\n193\tThe new branch must fork off the project's default branch (`origin/HEAD`), not\n194\toff whatever HEAD happens to be checked out — otherwise consecutive quick tasks\n195\tcompound on top of each other and stay unpushed (#2916). If `$branch_name`\n196\talready exists locally, reuse it as-is so resumed work is not rebased.\n197\t\n198\t```bash\n199\tDEFAULT_BRANCH=$(gsd_run query git.base-branch 2>/dev/null \\\n200\t  || git symbolic-ref --quiet --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null | sed 's|^origin/||' \\\n201\t  || echo main)\n202\t\n203\tif git show-ref --verify --quiet \"refs/heads/$branch_name\"; then\n204\t  git switch \"$branch_name\" \\\n205\t    || { echo \"ERROR: Could not switch to existing quick-task branch '$branch_name'.\" >&2; exit 1; }\n206\telse\n207\t  # Fetch the default branch so origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH is current. If the fetch\n208\t  # fails (offline, no remote, auth failure) AND we have no local copy of\n209\t  # origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH to fall back on, abort — creating the branch off\n210\t  # arbitrary HEAD is exactly the bug #2916 fixed.\n211\t  if ! git fetch --quiet origin \"$DEFAULT_BRANCH\"; then\n212\t    if ! git show-ref --verify --quiet \"refs/remotes/origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH\"; then\n213\t      echo \"ERROR: Could not fetch origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH and no local copy exists. Refusing to create '$branch_name' off the current HEAD (#2916). Resolve the remote/network issue and retry.\" >&2\n214\t      exit 1\n215\t    fi\n216\t    echo \"WARNING: git fetch origin $DEFAULT_BRANCH failed; using the local copy of origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH as base.\" >&2\n217\t  fi\n218\t\n219\t  if [ -n \"$(git status --porcelain)\" ]; then\n220\t    echo \"WARNING: Uncommitted changes present. Carrying them onto the new quick-task branch — they will be branched off origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH (not the previous-task HEAD).\"\n221\t  else\n222\t    # Best-effort: fast-forward the local default branch so subsequent local\n223\t    # work sees the latest tip. Failure here is non-fatal because we always\n224\t    # create the new branch directly from origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH below.\n225\t    git switch --quiet \"$DEFAULT_BRANCH\" 2>/dev/null \\\n226\t      && git merge --ff-only --quiet \"origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH\" 2>/dev/null \\\n227\t      || true\n228\t  fi\n229\t\n230\t  # Pin the new branch to origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH so the start point is\n231\t  # deterministic regardless of which branch we are currently on (#2916).\n232\t  # On success HEAD is exactly at origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH, so a post-creation\n233\t  # merge-base / \"ahead-of\" guard would be unreachable — the explicit base\n234\t  # argument here is the single source of correctness for #2916.\n235\t  # --no-track: with the default branch.autoSetupMerge=true, checkout -b from a\n236\t  # remote-tracking ref wires branch.<name>.merge to refs/heads/$DEFAULT_BRANCH\n237\t  # (origin/master), so a GUI sync pushes quick-task commits straight onto\n238\t  # origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH, bypassing PR review (#2498).\n239\t  git checkout -b \"$branch_name\" \"origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH\" --no-track \\\n240\t    || { echo \"ERROR: Could not create '$branch_name' from origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH (#2916).\" >&2; exit 1; }\n241\tfi\n242\t```\n243\t\n244\tAll quick-task commits for this run stay on that branch. User handles merge/rebase afterward.\n245\t\n246\t---\n247\t\n248\t**Step 3: Create task directory**\n249\t\n250\t```bash\n251\tmkdir -p \"${task_dir}\"\n252\t```\n253\t\n254\t---\n255\t\n256\t**Step 4: Create quick task directory**\n257\t\n258\tCreate the directory for this quick task:\n259\t\n260\t```bash\n261\tQUICK_DIR=\"${task_dir}\"\n262\tmkdir -p \"$QUICK_DIR\"\n263\t```\n264\t\n265\tReport to user:\n266\t```\n267\tCreating quick task ${quick_id}: ${DESCRIPTION}\n268\tDirectory: ${QUICK_DIR}\n269\t```\n270\t\n271\tStore `$QUICK_DIR` for use in orchestration.\n272\t\n273\t---\n274\t\n275\t**Step 4 ordering (#3894):** Check whether `workflow.research_before_questions` is enabled in `.planning/config.json` (or the config from init context) — the same check `/gsd-discuss-phase` and `/gsd-new-project` already make. Running it at startup prevents accumulation of orphaned worktrees from prior sessions that exited without cleanup (#3707).\n\n```bash\nif [ \"$USE_WORKTREES\" != \"false\" ]; then\n  gsd_run query worktree.reap-orphans 2>/dev/null || true\nfi\n```\n\nIf the project uses git submodules, worktree isolation is unsafe **only when the quick task touches a submodule path**. The previous behavior unconditionally disabled worktree isolation whenever `.gitmodules` existed, which penalised every quick task in a submodule project even when the task was nowhere near a submodule. Parse submodule paths from `.gitmodules` so the executor can act on actual submodule paths rather than the mere file's existence:\n\n```bash\n# Parse submodule paths from .gitmodules once (empty if no .gitmodules).\n# SUBMODULE_PATHS is a newline-separated list of repo-relative paths used as\n# a fail-loud commit-time guard inside the quick-task executor — if the\n# executor stages any path that falls inside SUBMODULE_PATHS, it must abort\n# the commit and surface the conflict rather than silently corrupting the\n# submodule state.\nif [ -f .gitmodules ]; then\n  SUBMODULE_PATHS=$(git config --file .gitmodules --get-regexp '^submodule\\..*\\.path$' 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $2}')\nelse\n  SUBMODULE_PATHS=\"\"\nfi\n```\n\nQuick mode does not have a pre-declared `files_modified` list (the task is freeform), so use a fail-loud guard at commit time: when the executor stages files for the quick-task commit, if any staged path falls inside a `SUBMODULE_PATHS` entry, abort with a clear error explaining that worktree-isolated commits cannot safely span submodule boundaries — the user can re-run with `workflow.use_worktrees=false` to fall back to sequential execution on the main tree. If `SUBMODULE_PATHS` is empty (no `.gitmodules` in the repo), worktree isolation proceeds normally.\n\n**If `roadmap_exists` is false:** Error — Quick mode requires an active project with ROADMAP.md. Run `/gsd-new-project` first.\n\nQuick tasks can run mid-phase - validation only checks ROADMAP.md exists, not phase status.\n\n---\n\n**Step 2.5: Handle quick-task branching**\n\n**If `branch_name` is empty/null:** Skip and continue on the current branch.\n\n**If `branch_name` is set:** Check out the quick-task branch before any planning commits.\n\nThe new branch must fork off the project's default branch (`origin/HEAD`), not\noff whatever HEAD happens to be checked out — otherwise consecutive quick tasks\ncompound on top of each other and stay unpushed (#2916). If `$branch_name`\nalready exists locally, reuse it as-is so resumed work is not rebased.\n\n```bash\nDEFAULT_BRANCH=$(gsd_run query git.base-branch 2>/dev/null \\\n  || git symbolic-ref --quiet --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null | sed 's|^origin/||' \\\n  || echo main)\n\nif git show-ref --verify --quiet \"refs/heads/$branch_name\"; then\n  git switch \"$branch_name\" \\\n    || { echo \"ERROR: Could not switch to existing quick-task branch '$branch_name'.\" >&2; exit 1; }\nelse\n  # Fetch the default branch so origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH is current. If the fetch\n  # fails (offline, no remote, auth failure) AND we have no local copy of\n  # origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH to fall back on, abort — creating the branch off\n  # arbitrary HEAD is exactly the bug #2916 fixed.\n  if ! git fetch --quiet origin \"$DEFAULT_BRANCH\"; then\n    if ! git show-ref --verify --quiet \"refs/remotes/origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH\"; then\n      echo \"ERROR: Could not fetch origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH and no local copy exists. Refusing to create '$branch_name' off the current HEAD (#2916). Resolve the remote/network issue and retry.\" >&2\n      exit 1\n    fi\n    echo \"WARNING: git fetch origin $DEFAULT_BRANCH failed; using the local copy of origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH as base.\" >&2\n  fi\n\n  if [ -n \"$(git status --porcelain)\" ]; then\n    echo \"WARNING: Uncommitted changes present. Carrying them onto the new quick-task branch — they will be branched off origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH (not the previous-task HEAD).\"\n  else\n    # Best-effort: fast-forward the local default branch so subsequent local\n    # work sees the latest tip. Failure here is non-fatal because we always\n    # create the new branch directly from origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH below.\n    git switch --quiet \"$DEFAULT_BRANCH\" 2>/dev/null \\\n      && git merge --ff-only --quiet \"origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH\" 2>/dev/null \\\n      || true\n  fi\n\n  # Pin the new branch to origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH so the start point is\n  # deterministic regardless of which branch we are currently on (#2916).\n  # On success HEAD is exactly at origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH, so a post-creation\n  # merge-base / \"ahead-of\" guard would be unreachable — the explicit base\n  # argument here is the single source of correctness for #2916.\n  # --no-track: with the default branch.autoSetupMerge=true, checkout -b from a\n  # remote-tracking ref wires branch.<name>.merge to refs/heads/$DEFAULT_BRANCH\n  # (origin/master), so a GUI sync pushes quick-task commits straight onto\n  # origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH, bypassing PR review (#2498).\n  git checkout -b \"$branch_name\" \"origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH\" --no-track \\\n    || { echo \"ERROR: Could not create '$branch_name' from origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH (#2916).\" >&2; exit 1; }\nfi\n```\n\nAll quick-task commits for this run stay on that branch. That belongs in an early performance spike.\n94\t\n95\t## The Four Named Tools\n96\t\n97\t### 1. motion-primitives (ibelick) : USE, as a copy-in source library. Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH\n98\t\n99\t- Only deps are `motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `lucide-react`, plus a `@/lib/utils` `cn()` helper. **No shadcn init required.**\n100\t- Components are served as shadcn-registry JSON at `https://motion-primitives.com/c/<name>.json` (HTTP 200 verified).\n101\t- The official CLI is `npx motion-primitives@latest add <name>`. It works (tested) but the npm package is stale (0.1.0, March 2025) and **drops files into `./components/motion-primitives/` at the project root, not `src/`**. Either move them to `src/components/motion-primitives/` or skip the CLI and copy the registry JSON content. Decide once and document it.\n102\t- Needs the `@` alias in both `vite.config.ts` (`resolve.alias`) and `tsconfig.app.json` (`paths: { \"@/*\": [\"./src/*\"] }`). With TS 6/7, `paths` works **without** `baseUrl` (verified in the probe). shadcn's Vite doc still says to add `baseUrl`. You do not need it.\n103\t\n104\t### 2. react-spring : USE, scoped. Confidence: HIGH\n105\t\n106\t- Install `@react-spring/web@~10.1.2`. Import `useSpring, useSprings, useTrail, useChain, useTransition, animated, config` from `@react-spring/web`.\n107\t- Version note: `react-spring` (the umbrella, 10.0.4) is behind and v11.0.0-beta (beta.1 released 2026-10-01) is **removing it**, going ESM-only, and deprecating `useTransition` in favor of new `usePresence`/`usePresenceList`. Stay on 10.1.x stable. Avoid `useTransition` for new core UI (use motion's `AnimatePresence`) so the v11 migration stays trivial.\n108\t- Reduced motion is built in: `useReducedMotion` is exported from `@react-spring/web` (confirmed in the type definitions), and the global flag `Globals.assign({ skipAnimation: true })` snaps every spring to its target. Wire it once (snippet below).\n109\t- Dependencies are tiny and tree-shakable. Measured at about +17 kB gz for `useSpring/useTrail/useSprings`.\n110\t\n111\t### 3. realtimecolors.com : USE as a design tool, with caveats. Confidence: HIGH\n112\t\n113\t- The seed (`050315 / fbfbfe / 2f27ce / dedcff / 433bff`, Inter/Inter) is Text, Background, Primary, Secondary, Accent. Note `050315` on `fbfbfe` is the **light** theme pairing (dark text on light bg). The tool's light/dark toggle (Alt+T) lets you design both modes in one session. The project requires light and dark, so design both explicitly rather than inverting.\n114\t- It shows AA/AAA contrast traffic lights per role. Use them as the accessibility gate for text and interactive colors.\n115\t- Exports: CSS variables, Tailwind CSS, SCSS, and custom templates, in HEX/RGB/HSL/OKLAB/OKLCH. The tool lists a `tailwind.config.js` style Tailwind export and does not mention v4. **Export \"CSS\" with OKLCH and paste into `@theme`**, not the Tailwind-config export:\n116\t- Its type-scale presets (1.067 to 1.618) map to a `--text-*` ladder in `@theme`.\n117\t- The user wants alternatives explored: do that in the design phase (Realtime Colors' scheme generators: analogous/complementary/triadic, plus randomize with Space). Keep exactly 5 role tokens plus derived tints so swapping palettes later is a single-block edit.\n118\t\n119\t### 4. godly.design/posts : USE as inspiration only, not a dependency. Confidence: MEDIUM\n120\t\n121\t- `godly.design/posts` is a curated **feed of linked social posts** (mostly X links to designers' UI interaction clips), with category nav (Websites, Tools, Templates, etc.). No dates, tags, RSS, or API were visible. Treat it as a mood-board source: capture screenshots/links into the planning docs, then extract motion patterns (spring feel, press states, cursor effects) into a written reference list before coding. (Probe also noted `godly.website` currently 301-redirects to `recent.design`, so the brand's structure may have shifted. Rely on `godly.design/posts/` and verify when you actually browse.)\n122\t- No code or package implications.\n123\t\n124\t## Division of Responsibility (motion vs react-spring)\n125\t\n126\t| Concern | Owner | Why |\n127\t|---------|-------|-----|\n128\t| Mount/unmount, `AnimatePresence`, exit animations | **motion** | Mature, handles React 19 strict mode and transitions (13.1.1 and 13.4.6 fixes). |\n129\t| Layout and shared-element transitions (`layout`, `layoutId`, Morphing Dialog) | **motion** | react-spring has no equivalent. |\n130\t| Scroll-linked values (`useScroll`, `useTransform`, ScrollProgress, in-view reveals) | **motion** | Already bundled. 13.4.x moved offsets onto hardware-accelerated `ViewTimeline` where supported. |\n131\t| Text/number effects, stagger reveals, all motion-primitives prefabs | **motion** | They are written against it. |\n132\t| Simple drag, `whileTap`, `whileHover` | **motion** | Built in. No extra gesture lib. |\n133\t| Velocity-carrying physics: flick/toss, drag-release with momentum, rubber-band, pointer-chasing follower, squish-on-press toys | **react-spring** | `useSpring` with continuous retargeting is its sweet spot and gives the \"tactile\" signature. |\n134\t| Staggered chains of springs (`useTrail`, `useChain`) for playful sets of elements | **react-spring** | Concise API. |\n135\t| Anything in `@react-spring/three` | **react-spring** | Only if 3D is adopted. |\n136\t\n137\t## Tailwind v4 Notes\n138\t\n139\t- v4 `hover:` only applies under `@media (hover: hover)`, so hover styles never stick after a tap on phones. This matches the \"no desktop-only gestures\" requirement. Do **not** restore v3 behavior with `@custom-variant hover (&:hover)`.\n140\t- Browser floor: Safari 16.4+, Chrome 111+, Firefox 128+ (uses `@property`, `color-mix()`). Fine for this audience.\n141\t- No `tailwind.config.js`; `tw-animate-css` (the shadcn replacement for tailwindcss-animate) is not needed since motion handles animation.\n142\t\n143\t## Dark Mode (covered: Tailwind v4 + tiny script)\n144\t\n145\t## Font Loading\n146\t\n147\t- `import '@fontsource-variable/inter/wght.css'` in `main.tsx`. Verified: it declares `font-display: swap`, `font-weight: 100 900`, and per-script `unicode-range`, so a browser downloads only the **latin subset (48 kB woff2)** for English copy (latin-ext is 85 kB and only fetched if used). Vite emits all subsets to `dist/` (harmless unused files).\n148\t- `@fontsource-variable/inter/opsz.css` adds optical sizing (latin 73 kB). Worth it only if you want display-size tuning.\n149\t- **Preload is not automatic**: a bare `<link rel=\"preload\" href=\"@fontsource-variable/inter/files/...\">` in `index.html` is *not* rewritten by Vite (verified, stays unresolved). If you want a preload, use a small `transformIndexHtml` plugin or `import url from '...woff2?url'`. Skipping preload is acceptable with `font-display: swap`; revisit if Lighthouse flags it.\n150\t- If the design adds a display face from Realtime Colors, use the same Fontsource route (one variable family, latin only), and keep to 2 families total for mobile performance.\n151\t\n152\t## GitHub Pages Deploy\n153\t\n154\t## Alternatives Considered\n155\t\n156\t| Category | Recommended | Alternative | Why Not |\n157\t|----------|-------------|-------------|---------|\n158\t| Framework | Vite + React | Next.js / Astro | Next explicitly out of scope.
